problem: Atomic cleanup tracked ownership only in memory; after another actor replaced the published version path, failure cleanup could delete foreign bytes.
cause: An owned_version boolean proved only that this process had once published the path, not that the current filesystem object was still the same object.
rule: Before destructive cleanup of a mutable shared path, revalidate a filesystem-resident unguessable ownership token immediately before deletion; an in-memory ownership flag alone never authorizes deletion.
applies_to: atomic imports, version directories, temporary publication paths, concurrent filesystem writers
